---

[[_TOC_]]

# Environment Variables

KWin supports a number of environment variables to overwrite some settings or checks.

## KWIN_COMPOSE

The environment variable **KWIN_COMPOSE** enforces a compositing backend. The following values are supported:

* _O_: OpenGL backend (either OpenGL 1, OpenGL 2 or OpenGL ES 2.0)
* _O1_: OpenGL 1 backend (only 4.x)
* _O2_: OpenGL 2 backend
* _O2ES_: OpenGL ES 2 backend (since 5.5)
* _Q_: QPainter backend (only Wayland)

Note that as of KWin 6.8, only OpenGL ES 2+ is supported.

## KWIN_LOG_PERFORMANCE_DATA

This drops performance data about each committed frame into a csv in the home folder, which can be useful for debugging or optimizations.

## KWIN_GL_DEBUG

By setting **KWIN_GL_DEBUG** to _1_ the OpenGL rendering can be debugged visually. All geometries which are rendered are overlayed by a wireframe. The wireframe is not available in OpenGL ES 2.0. The environment variable is supported since 4.7.

## KWIN_PERSISTENT_VBO

Performance feature that requires GL_ARB_sync and GL_ARB_buffer_storage extension to use a ring buffer instead of reallocating vertex buffer objects.

## KWIN_EFFECTS_FORCE_ANIMATIONS

Allows to force override whether animations should be forced on or off. The recommendation of the compositor will be override. This environment variable is supported since 5.8.

* "0" explicitly disable animations
* "1" explicitly enable animations

## KWIN_USE_BUFFER_AGE

Buffer age allows KWin to only repaint parts of the screen that actually changed in a given buffer vs. the current scene; this is enabled by default now, but you can disable it by setting the environment variable to zero.

## KWIN_WAYLAND_DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTION_BUFFER_SIZE

Can be set to change the default maximum client connection buffer size. The size is specified in bytes. The actual size of the connection buffers is a power of two, therefore the specified maximum buffer size will be rounded up to the nearest power of two as well.

By default, KWin sets the maximum connection buffer size to 1 MiB or 1048576 in bytes. A higher value can be set if there are clients that are terminated due to not processing events fast enough, but it also increases the chances of having high memory usage.

## KWIN_FORCE_SW_CURSOR

On Wayland set this variable to directly use a software rendered mouse cursor instead of trying to probe for a cursor plane. It is recommended to only set this environment variable for debugging and not set it in general because using a cursor plane improves performance and KWin should fall back to software rendered cursor in case it can not find a suitable cursor plane.

## KWIN_WAYLAND_NO_XAUTHORITY

Set to `1` to indicate that the Xwayland server should be started without Xauthority file. It is primarily intended for the debugging purposes and for bug triaging. This environment variable is available since 5.22.0.

## KWIN_DRM_NO_AMS

Makes kwin_wayland running on drm use the legacy driver interface

## KWIN_DRM_USE_MODIFIERS

Enable explicit modifiers for kwin_wayland running on drm. This option can improve screen rotation and efficiency but also breaks some display configurations at the moment.

## KWIN_DRM_NO_DIRECT_SCANOUT

Disables direct scanout for kwin_wayland, can be useful for debugging

## KWIN_DRM_PREFER_COLOR_DEPTH

Can be set to make kwin_wayland and applications prefer a given color bits per pixel. 30 (10 bits per color) is the default, 24 reverts it to 8 bits per color channel.

## KWIN_DRM_DEVICES

Can be set to explicitly tell kwin_wayland which GPU(s) to use. The format is a colon-separated list, like this: `/dev/dri/card1:/dev/dri/card0`. As the `card*` file order is not stable, using the symlinks in `/dev/dri/by-path` is also supported, like this: `KWIN_DRM_DEVICES="/dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000\:03\:00.0-card:/dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000\:59\:00.0-card"` (note that the colons in the file name are escaped with `\`).

The first device in the list will be used by KWin and most apps for rendering.

## KWIN_DRM_DISABLE_BUFFER_READABILITY_CHECKS

Can be set to 1 to make KWin not check for buffer readability before submitting buffers to the kernel, or to 0 to enable the buffer readability checks. The checks are disabled by default for the i915 Intel kernel driver, as it caused performance issues and lags on some Intel systems.

## KWIN_DRM_ALLOW_INTEL_COLORSPACE

Enables support for the `Colorspace` drm property and HDR on Intel. This is disabled by default, because the Intel implementation of the property is currently broken

## KWIN_DRM_ALLOW_NVIDIA_COLORSPACE

Enables support for the `Colorspace` drm property and HDR on NVidia GPUs. This is disabled by default for some driver versions because of [BUG 488941](https://bugs.kde.org/show_bug.cgi?id=488941)

## KWIN_DRM_NO_DCC_WORKAROUND

Allows KWin to use non-linear modifiers for color management on AMD. This is off by default because DCC modifiers currently cause glitches: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/issues/10875

## KWIN_DRM_DISABLE_TRIPLE_BUFFERING

Can be set to 1 to disable triple buffering on Wayland.

## KWIN_WAYLAND_EMULATE_TABLET

Can be set to 1 to make KWin emulate tablet input as pointer input if an application provides no support for tablets.

## KWIN_DPMS_WORKAROUND_TIMEOUT

Can be set to a value in milliseconds to work around displays that temporarily disconnect while being in power saving mode; if it reconnects in less than the time specified by this variable, KWin will keep the display off until user interaction rather than immediately enabling it again.

The default is 2000.

## KWIN_DRM_OVERRIDE_SAFETY_MARGIN

Overrides the safety margin, in microseconds, which may help with performance issues when the CPU in the system is especially slow and the driver takes too long. The issue usually manifests in only getting half the refresh rate of what you set the screen to.

The default is 1000.

## KWIN_IM_SHOW_ALWAYS

Makes the virtual keyboard show even if you didn't use touch to focus a text field.

## KWIN_WAYLAND_REENABLE_WL_DRM

Re-enables the wl_drm protocol, in case any software still breaks without it.

## KWIN_X11_NO_SYNC_REQUEST

Set to `1` to disable synchronized resizing for Xwayland windows.

## KWIN_USE_OVERLAYS

Set to `1` to enable overlay plane usage, and `0` to disable it. Currently the feature is disabled by default for release builds, and enabled by default for development versions.

## KWIN_DISABLE_TONEMAPPING

Set to `1` to disable tone mapping of HDR content, for testing or to work around broken games.

## KWIN_DISABLE_VULKAN

Set to `1` to disable the use of Vulkan in KWin for debugging purposes.

## KWIN_DISABLE_UDMABUF_IMPORT
Set to `1` to disable importing shm buffers with udmabuf.

## KWIN_XKB_DEFAULT_KEYMAP

This environment variable forces the xkb integration on Wayland to use a default keymap instead of using the configured one. Mostly required for testing. This environment variable is supported since 5.8.

## KWIN_DEVICE_SKIPS_INPUT_METHOD

If we have a grabbing input method, it by default takes all input. This comma separated list allows you to mark some devices as not wanting to be processed via the input method.
Find the device ID through the kwin debug console.

## KWIN_DRM_USE_COLOR_PIPELINE

Set to `0` to disable the use of drm color pipelines, and `1` to enable them.

## KWIN_IM_WAYLAND_DEBUG

Set to `1` to enable WAYLAND_DEBUG for the input method.

## KWIN_WAYLAND_SUPPORT_COMMIT_TIMING_V1

Set to `0` to disable the wp-commit-timing-v1 support.

It can be useful for debugging performance issues in video games.

# Set variables at session start

* Create a script file `kwin_env.sh` with the variables you wish to set.

---

# Usage

Create a file as per:

```shell
#!/bin/sh

export FOO=bar
export BAR=foo
```

* Make the script executable (file properties or `chmod +x kwin_vars.sh`)
* Place the script in a sourced path

Then copy to `~/.config/plasma-workspace/env/`.

Minimal fix: hold one decon_activate_vsync() reference for the pipe lifetime (enable/disable), stop using the raw uncounted arm, re-point the DRM event path at the existing (currently dead) arm helper, and remove the double drm_handle_vblank().

data.architecture: Vendor video-mode model: DECON scans out RGB to DSIM; the FRAME IRQ (SPI 202/IRQ 234) is enabled only on demand by decon_activate_vsync() -> decon_reg_set_int(en=1) [VIDINTCON0=0x8803] + DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1) [unmask DSIM_INTMSK FRAME_DONE], and is disabled by decon_deactivate_vsync() -> decon_reg_set_int(en=0) [clears only INT_ENABLE, 0x8802] + DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(0). decon_wait_for_vsync() brackets every wait with that pair, so the line is armed only for the duration of a wait; nothing in the vendor keeps it armed permanently and decon_enable() does not arm it at all in video mode. The handler acks by writing 1 to VIDINTCON1.INT_FRAME (W1C), then timestamps and wakes decon->vsync_info.wait; our patched handler additionally calls kms_vblank_cb outside decon->slock. Our shim writes the same VIDINTCON0 value but outside the refcount, so each vendor wait our own commit performs ends by clearing INT_ENABLE and DSIM's mask, and DRM's vblank reference (enable_vblank) touches no hardware. Fix by giving KMS the lifetime reference and by actually arming DRM events instead of completing them at commit time.
data.report:
# DECON FRAME/VSYNC interrupt: vendor reference vs our KMS driver

All vendor citations are the tree we build (`scratch-k94`), which already carries the 0100 shim patch; the pristine vendor tree has the same bodies at slightly earlier line numbers. Ours = `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/`.

Configuration facts first, because they decide the whole question:

* `exynos7580-j7elte_rev04.dts:1009-1017`: `psr_mode = <0>` (**DECON_VIDEO_MODE**), `trig_mode = <1>` (SW trigger). Our DSI encoder even refuses anything else (`exynos_drm7580_dsi.c:90-94`).
* `exynos7580-q.dtsi:990-992`: `interrupts = <0 203 0>, <0 201 0>, <0 202 0>;` with the comment `int_0: fifo_irq, int_1: cmd_mode_irq, int_2: frame_done_irq`. With the GIC SPI base 32 that is **IRQ 235 = FIFO**, **IRQ 233 = I80/cmd**, **IRQ 234 = frame_done (video mode)**.
* `decon_int_register_irq()` (`decon-int_drv.c:785-819`) always requests resource **0** (FIFO) and then, for `psr_mode == DECON_VIDEO_MODE`, resource **2** — the frame_done line — with `devm_request_irq(dev, res->start, decon_int_irq_handler, 0, pdev->name, decon)` (`:813-815`). Command mode takes resource 1 instead (`:803-806`).
* All of them use the **same action name** (`pdev->name` = `14830000.decon_fb`), so `/proc/interrupts` prints **two lines with that label** (234 frame, 235 fifo). The FIFO/underrun line is *supposed* to stay at 0 on a healthy pipe.

So: in this configuration vblank **must** come from DECON, SPI 202 / Linux IRQ 234, not from DSIM. DSIM's own IRQ (`14800000.dsim`) is only unmasked as a side effect of `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC` and is not the vendor's vblank source (see §4).

---

## 1. Every vendor write that enables the FRAME/VSYNC interrupt

| # | Vendor site | What it writes | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `decon-reg_7580.c:569-590` `decon_reg_set_int(en=1)` | `decon_write_mask(VIDINTCON0, val, ~0)` with `val = INT_ENABLE(1<<0) \| FIFOLEVEL_EMPTY(0<<3) \| INT_FIFO(1<<1) \| INT_FRAME(1<<11) \| FRAMESEL0_VSYNC(1<<15)` = **0x00008803** (video mode); command mode instead uses `INT_ENABLE \| FIFOLEVEL_EMPTY \| INT_FIFO \| INT_I80_EN(1<<17)` and first W1C-clears `VIDINTCON1.INT_I80` (`:581-582`) | the only place the frame interrupt is enabled |
| 2 | `decon_reg_7580.c:593-597` `decon_reg_set_int(en=0)` | `decon_write_mask(VIDINTCON0, 0, VIDINTCON0_INT_ENABLE)` | clears **only** bit 0; FRAME/FRAMESEL/FIFO bits stay set (readback 0x8802) |
| 3 | `decon_core.c:1189-1211` `decon_activate_vsync()` | `if (!irq_refcount++) { if (psr_mode == VIDEO) { decon_reg_set_int(...,1); v4l2_subdev_call(..., DSIM_IOC_VSYNC, 1); } }` | refcounted arm; the 0->1 edge is the only time hardware is touched |
| 4 | `decon_core.c:1213-1236` `decon_deactivate_vsync()` | `if (!--irq_refcount) { decon_reg_set_int(...,0); DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(0); }` | refcounted disarm, **including** the VIDINTCON0 bit-0 clear |
| 5 | `decon_reg_7580.c:314-320` `decon_reg_clear_int()` | `decon_write_mask(VIDINTCON1, 0, INT_I80\|INT_FRAME\|INT_FIFO)` | W1C of stale pending bits; called at the end of `decon_reg_init()` (`:444`) and in `decon_disable()` (`decon_core.c:1085`) |
| 6 | `decon-int_drv.c:105-106` | `decon_write_mask(VIDINTCON1, ~0, VIDINTCON1_INT_FRAME)` | per-IRQ acknowledge (W1C bit 1) |
| 7 | `dsim_drv.c:86-131` + `dsim_reg_7580.c:1001-1011` | `dsim_reg_set_int(en)`: `val = en ? 0 : ~0` into `DSIM_INTMSK` masked with `SFR_PL_FIFO_EMPTY \| SFR_PH_FIFO_EMPTY \| FRAME_DONE \| RX_DATA_DONE \| RX_ECC` | `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1/0)` unmasks/masks the DSIM interrupt set (refcounted separately in `dsim->irq_refcount`) |
| 8 | `decon-int_drv.c:792-796` | `devm_request_irq(res 0, decon_int_irq_handler, flags=0, pdev->name)`; `:813-815` same for res 2 in video mode | GIC level IRQ (DT trigger cell 0 => GIC default level-high), shared action name |

**TRIGCON is not part of the video-mode interrupt path at all.** `decon_reg_configure_trigger()`/`decon_reg_set_trigger()` are called only under `if (psr->psr_mode == DECON_MIPI_COMMAND_MODE)` in `decon_reg_init()` (`decon_reg_7580.c:440-441`), `decon_reg_init_probe()` (`:476-477`) and `decon_reg_start()` (`:486-489`, HW-trigger command mode only); `decon_reg_stop()`/`decon_update_regs()` mask it for HW-trigger command mode (`decon_core.c:1964-1966`, `:2187-2194`). In video mode nothing programs TRIGCON, so **`TRIGCON=0x40` (= reset default `HWTRIG_AUTO_MASK`) is expected** and identical to the working dump in `decon-kms-int74.md:11` (`VIDINTCON0=0x8803, FRAME IRQ firing, TRIGCON=0x40, VIDCON0=0x7`). It is a red herring.

### Ack/serve sequence (vendor, video mode)

```
IRQ 234 (SPI 202) -> decon_int_irq_handler (decon-int_drv.c:78)
  spin_lock(decon->slock)
  if state == OFF || LPD: goto end            (:90-92; still IRQ_HANDLED, /proc still counts)
  sts = read VIDINTCON1                       (:94)
  if sts & INT_FRAME(0x2):                    (:102)
      write VIDINTCON1 = 1<<1                 (:105-106)  <- W1C acknowledge
      vsync_info.timestamp = ktime_get()      (:107)
      wake_up(vsync_info.wait)                (:109)
      kms_frame = true
  if sts & INT_FIFO(0x1):  ... ack bit0       (:111-127)
  if sts & INT_I80(0x4):   ... ack bit2       (:128-133)
  spin_unlock(decon->slock)
  if kms_frame && kms_vblank_cb: cb(data)     (:144-145)  <- our DRM entry
  return IRQ_HANDLED                          (:147)
```

There is **no enable bit in VIDINTCON1** — it is status/W1C only. `INTEN` = `VIDINTCON0[0]`, `INT_FRAME` = `VIDINTCON0[11]`, `FRAMESEL0` = `VIDINTCON0[15:13]`.

### The lifecycle that matters

`decon_enable()` in video mode writes **no** VIDINTCON0 at all (`decon_core.c:1000-1012` is inside `if (psr_mode != DECON_VIDEO_MODE)`), and `decon_disable()` likewise only touches it in command mode (`:1061-1068`). The only video-mode arming is the `decon_activate_vsync()` 0->1 edge, reached from `decon_wait_for_vsync()` (`decon_core.c:1253-1254`) and from the `S3CFB_SET_VSYNC_INT` ioctl (`:1311-1314`). `decon_wait_for_vsync()` **always** calls `decon_deactivate_vsync()` afterwards (`:1267-1268`), and `decon_update_regs()` calls `decon_wait_for_vsync()` once per frame (`:2165` for `kms_owned`, `:2171` for fbdev). So even on stock fbdev the line is armed only while somebody is inside a vsync wait — that is the vendor's design, and it proves the hardware line works at 60 Hz in video mode (every stock frame update blocks on it).

---

## 2. Register-by-register: vendor vs ours

Our values are the ones in the ticket, produced by our shim's `decon_kms_log_state()`/`decon_kms_dump_regs()` (`decon_kms_api.c:661-684`, `:707-731`).

| Register | Vendor, video mode | Where the vendor sets it | Ours | Missing / wrong? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `VIDCON0` 0x0000 | `ENVID \| ENVID_F` (=0x3) after `decon_reg_direct_on_off(1)`; bit2 `DECON_STOP_STATUS` reads 1 while the pipe runs (that is what `decon_reg_wait_stop_status_timeout()` waits to clear) | `decon_reg_7580.c:186-190`, `:483` | `0x00000007` | **No.** Same as the working dump (`int74`). If bit2 were 0 with ENVID=1 the pipe would not be scanning, but 0x7 = scanning. |
| `VIDOUTCON0` 0x0004 | `LCD_ON_F(1<<24)`, `IF_MASK(1<<23)=0` => RGB IF | `decon_reg_7580.c:56-68` | `0x01000000` | **No.** |
| `VIDINTCON0` 0x0500 | `INT_ENABLE(1<<0) \| INT_FIFO(1<<1) \| FIFOLEVEL_EMPTY(0<<3) \| INT_FRAME(1<<11) \| FRAMESEL0_VSYNC(1<<15)` = **0x8803** | `decon_reg_7580.c:578-590` via `decon_activate_vsync()` `decon_core.c:1196-1202` | `0x00008803` | **Bit-identical — nothing missing.** The bug is *when* it holds (see §3). |
| `VIDINTCON1` 0x0504 | status only (W1C): bit0 FIFO, bit1 FRAME, bit2 I80; cleared at init/stop, bit1 acked in the ISR | `decon_reg_7580.c:314-320`, `decon-int_drv.c:105-106` | `0x00000000` | **No**, but we never pre-ack a stale pending bit before arming (vendor only does it at init). Optional hardening. |
| `TRIGCON` 0x06B0 | *not written in video mode* (command mode only: `SWTRIGEN`/`HWTRIGEN\|HWTRIG_AUTO_MASK\|TRIG_SAVE_DISABLE`) | `decon_reg_7580.c:201-216`, `:440-441`, `:486-489`, `:604-613` | `0x00000040` (reset `HWTRIG_AUTO_MASK`) | **No.** Matches the working dump. |
| `DECON_UPDATE` 0x0710 | `STANDALONE_F` written after start and per commit, polled by `decon_reg_wait_for_update_timeout()` | `decon_reg_7580.c:180-183`, `:485`, `:626+` | not in the dump | No (handled by the vendor body we call). |
| Shadow protect | `decon_reg_shadow_protect_win()` around window writes | `decon_reg_7580.c:520-540`, `decon_core.c:1950-2098` | via the vendor | No. |
| DSIM `INTMSK` | `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1)` writes 0 into `FRAME_DONE\|SFR_PL/PH_FIFO_EMPTY\|RX_DATA_DONE\|RX_ECC` | `dsim_reg_7580.c:1001-1011` | not dumped | *Toggled* by our arm (unmasked) but masked again by every vendor wait's `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(0)`. |

**Conclusion of the comparison:** there is no unset enable bit, no un-acked status bit and no missing TRIGCON arm. A register-level "set bit X" patch cannot fix this, because the vendor's own working state is exactly 0x8803/0x40/0x7.

---

## 3. What our KMS driver is actually missing

1. **The arm has no owner.** `decon_kms_register_vblank_cb()` (`decon_kms_api.c:899-927`) only stores the callback ("int72: registration only stores the callback") and `exynos7580_enable_vblank()` (`exynos_drm7580_main.c:128-137`) only does `atomic_inc(&exynos7580_vblank_users)` with the comment "The FRAME interrupt is already armed from ->load()" — which is no longer true. So the DRM vblank reference (`drm_vblank_get()` on every armed flip event) keeps **nothing** enabled.
2. **Our own commit disarms it.** `decon_kms_commit()` (`decon_kms_api.c:779-812`) does `arm(:781) -> decon_export_update_regs(:782)` and the vendor body behind that is `decon_update_regs()` (`:1032-1040` -> `decon_core.c:2100`), which calls `decon_wait_for_vsync(decon, 100)` (`decon_core.c:2165`). That function brackets the sleep with `decon_activate_vsync()` / `decon_deactivate_vsync()` (`:1253-1268`), and the deactivate path executes `decon_reg_set_int(...,0)` -> `decon_write_mask(VIDINTCON0, 0, INT_ENABLE)` -> **0x8802** plus `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(0)` -> `dsim_reg_set_int(0)` which **masks** `DSIM_INTMSK`. The shim's own comment states this (`decon_kms_api.c:788-793`: "the wait's deactivate clears VIDINTCON0, so no new interrupt arrives"). Because `decon_kms_arm_frame()` writes VIDINTCON0 *outside* `decon->vsync_info.irq_refcount`, the value it installed is not protected and is clobbered by the next wait.
3. **Consequence chain.** After a commit whose internal wait is the last VIDINTCON0 writer (the 5-failure branch at `decon_kms_api.c:805-809`, or any vendor-internal wait), the line sits at 0x8802 = interrupt disabled, and `/proc/interrupts` for the frame line stops moving. Our flip event is still completed immediately (`fence.c:214-234`), so userspace keeps going and nobody notices. `drm_atomic_helper_wait_for_vblanks()` (`fence.c:302-303`) then times out at 50 ms per commit and the DRM vblank counter never advances.
4. **The DRM arming path is dead code.** `exynos7580_arm_vblank_event()` (`fence.c:140-149`) is the correct 3.10 equivalent of `drm_crtc_arm_vblank_event()` and is **never called**; `exynos7580_complete_crtc_event()` jumps straight to `exynos7580_send_event_now(drm, -1, e)` (`:214-234`, the int109/int110 workaround). So even with a live FRAME IRQ, no event would ever be delivered by it.
5. **Double count.** `exynos7580_vblank_isr()` (`main.c:115-125`) calls `drm_handle_vblank()` **and** `exynos7580_vblank_irq()` (`fence.c:320-330`), which calls `drm_handle_vblank()` again -> the cooked counter advances by 2 per FRAME interrupt once the IRQ works.
6. **Optional hardening:** ack a stale `VIDINTCON1.INT_FRAME` before arming (the vendor only does it in `decon_reg_init()`/`decon_reg_stop()`), otherwise an already-latched bit fires the handler immediately after enabling.

Things that are *not* the problem (checked and ruled out): VIDINTCON0 bits, FRAMESEL0 value, TRIGCON, IRQ trigger type (vendor uses flags 0 / GIC level for the same DT cell), `decon_disable()` masking the line (it does nothing to VIDINTCON0 in video mode), and `decon->irq` (= the ESD GPIO from `gpio_to_irq()`, `decon-int_drv.c:845-848` — the `disable_irq(decon->irq)` in `decon_disable()`/suspend paths touches the ESD line, not SPI 202).

---

## 4. Which block is expected to deliver vblank here

Video mode (`psr_mode=0`, DT `exynos7580-j7elte_rev04.dts:1012`; panel `lcd->mode == DECON_VIDEO_MODE` is enforced by `exynos_drm7580_dsi.c:90-94`):

* **DECON, SPI 202 = Linux IRQ 234**, handler registered by `decon_int_register_irq()` resource index 2 (`decon-int_drv.c:811-815`) under the name `14830000.decon_fb`. This is the vendor's video-mode vblank: it is where `decon_wait_for_vsync()` is woken from, i.e. every stock fbdev frame update depends on it.
* **Not DSIM.** The vendor only registers the *I80* handler (resource 1, SPI 201) for command mode. `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC` is called next to the DECON arming, but it only toggles `DSIM_INTMSK` (`dsim_reg_7580.c:1001-1011`); the `14800000.dsim` line that "advances at 60 Hz" is DSIM's own frame-done/FIFO-empty traffic and is **not** a DECON vblank — driving `drm_handle_vblank()` from it would timestamp the DRM pipe from a different block's phase.
* Because the FIFO/underrun line (SPI 203 = IRQ 235) and the frame line (SPI 202 = IRQ 234) share the action name, `/proc/interrupts` shows **two `14830000.decon_fb` lines**. The count that must move at ~60 Hz is **234**; **235 staying at 0 is correct** on a healthy pipe. Verify with `grep decon_fb /proc/interrupts` and watch which of the two changes.

If (and only if) IRQ 234 is proven silent while `VIDINTCON0` still reads 0x8803 *and* the pipe is scanning (`VIDCON0 & 0x3 == 0x3`), the fallback source would be the DSIM frame-done interrupt (`DSIM_INTMSK_FRAME_DONE`, unmasked by holding a `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1)` reference like `decon_activate_vsync()` does), or a `VIDCON1.LINECNT`-based software vblank. Neither is the vendor design and both are worse than fixing the arm lifetime; the vendor evidence (identical registers, working fbdev at 60 Hz, `int73/int74` dumps) says the DECON line does fire on this board.

---

## 5. Minimal patch

Register-wise nothing needs to be added. The three changes that make the frame IRQ fire continuously and make DRM use it:

**(P1) Hold one vsync reference for the pipe lifetime — `decon_kms_api.c:591-595` (in `decon_kms_enable()`, right after `decon_enable()` returns 0):**

```c
/* Replace the uncounted decon_kms_arm_frame() here.  The vendor only
 * enables VIDINTCON0 while a vsync reference is held; keeping one
 * reference for the whole pipe lifetime makes every vendor
 * decon_deactivate_vsync() a no-op (refcount 1 -> 0 only on disable),
 * so the FRAME IRQ stays enabled across commits and its own waits. */
if (decon->pdata->psr_mode == DECON_VIDEO_MODE && d->vblank_cb)
        decon_activate_vsync(decon);          /* 0 -> 1: VIDINTCON0=0x8803,
                                               * DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1) */
```

Exact resulting hardware state, verified by the vendor code path: `decon_reg_set_int(...,1)` at `decon_core.c:1200` -> `VIDINTCON0 = 0x8803`, `dsim_reg_set_int(1)` at `dsim_drv.c:102`/`:1157` -> `DSIM_INTMSK` FRAME_DONE bit cleared. `decon_wait_for_vsync()` inside commits then sees `prev_refcount == 1`, writes nothing, and its `decon_deactivate_vsync()` sees `new_refcount == 1`, so neither the DECON enable bit nor the DSIM mask is touched: **VIDINTCON0 stays 0x8803 for the whole session**.

**(P2) Balance it on the way down — `decon_kms_api.c` `decon_kms_disable()` (~:671-694, before `decon_disable(decon)`):**

```c
if (decon->pdata->psr_mode == DECON_VIDEO_MODE)
        decon_deactivate_vsync(decon);        /* 1 -> 0: 0x8802 + DSIM mask */
```

**(P3) Delete the uncounted arm, or leave it only as a readback check — `decon_kms_api.c:613-652` + call sites `:593`, `:781`, `:796`, `:803`.** `decon_kms_arm_frame()` writes `VIDINTCON0` without the refcount and calls `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1)` without a matching `(0)`, which leaks `dsim->irq_refcount` upward. With P1 held it is redundant; keeping it is harmless only if the `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1)` call is removed (the `decon_reg_set_int(...,1)` write is idempotent). Minimal textual patch: drop the `v4l2_subdev_call(... DSIM_IOC_VSYNC, 1)` block at `:641-645` and either drop the remaining body or keep the two `decon_info()` readbacks as diagnostics.

**(P4) Make DRM use the interrupt.**

* `exynos_drm7580_main.c:115-125`: delete the first `drm_handle_vblank(ex->drm, EXYNOS7580_PIPE)` — call only `exynos7580_vblank_irq(ex->drm, EXYNOS7580_PIPE)` (which is `drm_handle_vblank`, `fence.c:320-330`), otherwise the counter advances twice per frame.
* `exynos_drm7580_main.c:128-137` `enable_vblank()`: nothing more is needed once P1 holds, but the comment must be corrected; if you prefer defence in depth, re-assert `decon_reg_set_int(...,1)` here (it cannot clear anything).

* *What does the vendor do?* It requests the frame IRQ on DT interrupt index 2 (SPI 202/IRQ 234) only in video mode, enables it **only** through the refcounted `decon_activate_vsync()` -> `VIDINTCON0 = 0x8803` (+ `DSIM_IOC_VSYNC(1)`), serves it by reading `VIDINTCON1`, W1C-acking bit 1, timestamping and waking `vsync_info.wait`, and disables it through `decon_deactivate_vsync()` -> `VIDINTCON0 &= ~INT_ENABLE`. No TRIGCON involvement in video mode.
* *What are we missing?* Not a bit: the same 0x8803/0x40/0x7. # Screen bring-up: everything tried, and what it did

Two sessions: 2026-11-17 → 11-27 (GPU/KMS bring-up) and 2026-11-27 (this one).
Purpose: stop re-running ideas that did not change the panel.

## Changed the panel (keep these)

| Change | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| DECON KMS driver + DSI panel bring-up | Modeset works, panel lights, scanout latches (register dumps show `ADD0` follows the programmed fb) |
| int122: blank decision **before** `decon_kms_commit` + `last_fb[]` pinning | Blue/black **flashing stopped** (30/30 and 40/40 photos identical) |
| int126: bound `fb_shadow_write` by the shadow size; cache only frames ≥320×480 | Fixed `Unable to handle kernel paging request` in `exynos7580_fb_shadow_write+0x7c` that killed KWin's commit thread after one frame; KWin then committed 36+ frames |
| `modetest -s 21:720x1280` | Proved the panel follows DECON (blue → black); the DSI/panel is not stuck |
| KWIN_USE_BUFFER_AGE=0 (+ KWIN_FORCE_SW_CURSOR=1) | Removed the blue↔black alternation in the software session (8/8 photos identical), but the frame is near-black — no UI yet |

## Did not change the panel (discarded)

| Attempt | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Wallpaper plugin `org.kde.image`, re-apply + plasmashell restart | Good frame for a while (full repaint), then alternation returns |
| powerdevil / brightness writes (`/sys/class/backlight/panel`) | Nothing; AMOLED, the node is bogus (`actual 500 > max 355`) |
| `KWIN_COMPOSE=Q` (QPainter) | KWin exits: mode unsupported in 6.8 |
| `KWIN_COMPOSE=O2` vs `O2ES` | Same fragment-job hang / same crash |
| Blank heuristics: all-zero, uniform, ≤3 colours, 90 % near-black | Either let clear frames through or froze the panel on a stale shadow |
| `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=kms_swrast` alone | GBM still allocated panfrost buffers → untouched (zero) frames |
| `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=swrast` without dumb-buffer support | `DRM_IOCTL_MODE_CREATE_DUMB failed: Function not implemented` |
| `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE` with GBM on renderD128 | No dumb buffers until panfrost `dumb_create` was added |
| `LP_NUM_THREADS=0` | Made frames synchronous but did not produce client content |
| `GALLIUM_DRIVER=softpipe` | KWin survives (llvmpipe crashes), but frames still black |
| `QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software` for plasmashell | Shell loads the mobile-shell QML, still paints nothing visible |
| `fb0` writes / `fbtest` | No effect (CRTC keeps its own fb; fbtest wedged in D state) |
| Kernel panfrost `TIMEOUT-DIAG` + MMU/GPU IRQ unmask | No behaviour change; revealed the fault: `AS0 FAULTSTATUS=0x090002c3 FAULTADDRESS=0x0b2aa000`, `tiler did not idle` |
| `dumb_create`/`dumb_map_offset` in panfrost | Made kms_swrast+GBM viable (720×1292 dumb buffers), no UI yet |
| glibc `LD_PRELOAD` crash handler | Would not load (musl); rebuilt with device gcc |

## Diagnosed but not yet fixed

| Finding | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Fragment job never retires | `js ACTIVE(0x08)`, `head==tail`, `stat=rawstat=0`, full-screen 44×79 tiles, constant fault `0x0b2aa000` outside every BO in ERR-MAP |
| Tiler never idles | `pf7580: tiler did not idle on power-off, aborting suspend` after every recovery |
| KWin composited frames are clear-only | every 720×1280 commit samples 99.9 % black + cursor pixels; client content missing under both panfrost and software |
| DECON FRAME IRQ never armed for the pipe lifetime | vendor arms/disarms only around `decon_wait_for_vsync`; our shim bypasses the refcount → line mostly disarmed |
| llvmpipe crash | SIGSEGV at `libgallium-26.3.0.so+0x6cb5d0`, NULL destination write (only llvmpipe, not softpipe) |
| Mesa 20.3.5 stack missing | `/data/mesabuild/...` deleted; symlinks in `/data/mesa20sel` dangle. The 151 fps validation used that build |

## Open experiments (in flight)

1. Rebuild Mesa 20.3.5 for aarch64 musl and run KWin+plasmashell on panfrost (validated stack).
2. Compare vendor kbase (`drivers/gpu/arm/midgard`) with our panfrost port for the fragment-job/AS/tiler-heap difference.
3. Hold the DECON FRAME IRQ armed for the CRTC lifetime and deliver real vblank events.

content.text:
# /data/mesa203-env.sh - select the Mesa 20.3.5 (panfrost/kmsro) stack.
#
#   . /data/mesa203-env.sh          # render-node mode (renderD128, panfrost)
#   . /data/mesa203-env.sh kms      # card0/GBM mode (KWin: exynos -> kmsro -> panfrost)
#   . /data/mesa203-env.sh system   # back to the stock Mesa 26.3 (no-op reset)
#
# Source it in the shell that execs the program: LD_LIBRARY_PATH /
# LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH are read by the loader inside the process.
#
# Mesa 20.3.5 is the userspace that speaks this port's v5.2 panfrost UAPI;
# the system Mesa 26 submits a fragment job that never retires on this driver.
MESA203_PREFIX=/data/mesa203-install
export MESA203_PREFIX

case "${1:-render}" in
system)
	unset LD_LIBRARY_PATH LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH GBM_BACKENDS_PATH
	unset MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE EGL_PLATFORM
	LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH=/usr/lib/dri
	export LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH
	printf 'mesa203-env: system Mesa (%s)\n' "$(ls /usr/lib/libEGL.so.1* 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
	return 0 2>/dev/null || exit 0
	;;
kms)
	# card0 is the exynos/DECON KMS node: without the override the loader
	# picks exynos_dri.so, which is the kmsro entry point, and kmsro opens
	# the render node named "panfrost" for the actual 3D work.
	unset MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE
	;;
*)
	# Render node only: force panfrost_dri.so even on kernels whose DRM
	# driver is still named panfrost7580 (pre-rename images).
	MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=panfrost
	export MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE
	;;
esac

# libEGL.so.1, libGLESv2.so.2, libGLESv1_CM.so.1, libgbm.so.1,
# libglapi.so.0, libGL.so.1 live here.
LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$MESA203_PREFIX/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# panfrost_dri.so / exynos_dri.so (one gallium megadriver, 22 names).
LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH="$MESA203_PREFIX/lib/dri"
export LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH

# Not used by 20.3.5 (split gbm backends arrived in Mesa 22); exported so the
# same environment also works if a newer gbm is ever layered in.
GBM_BACKENDS_PATH="$MESA203_PREFIX/lib/dri"
export GBM_BACKENDS_PATH

# Neutralise a stale llvmpipe / PRIME / EGL_PLATFORM environment. This build
# has no llvmpipe at all (gallium-drivers=panfrost,kmsro).
unset LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE DRI_PRIME PAN_MESA_DEBUG EGL_PLATFORM

KWin fails to load: libkwin.so.6 requires `gbm_bo_create_with_modifiers2` and `gbm_bo_get_fd_for_plane` — symbols from Mesa's **libgbm ≥ 21**. Mesa 20.3.5's libgbm lacks them.

So KWin 6.8 cannot run with Mesa 20.3.5's libgbm. Workaround: keep the **system libgbm 26.3** but use Mesa 20.3.5's libEGL/libGLESv2/panfrost_dri? Mixing libgbm 26 with libEGL 20.3 is risky but might work: libgbm and libEGL are separate; KWin calls gbm_* from libgbm (26) and EGL from libEGL (20.3). The GBM backend loads the DRI driver (20.3 panfrost) via the loader; the EGL/GBM interaction uses the DRI interface.

Approach: set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to 20.3 libs but **exclude libgbm.so.1** (let it resolve from /usr/lib = 26.3). Since LD_LIBRARY_PATH takes precedence, we can create a directory with symlinks to 20.3 libs except libgbm, and use that.

The mesa203-install/lib contains libgbm.so.1 (20.3). If we make /data/mesa203-kwin/lib with symlinks to libEGL, libGLESv2, libGL, libglapi (20.3) but NOT libgbm, and set LD_LIBRARY_PATH there + LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH to 20.3 dri, the loader will find libgbm from the system.

Risk: Mesa 20.3's libEGL and Mesa 26's libgbm both load the DRI driver; version mismatch may break.

Alternative: patch KWin to not require those GBM symbols? No.

Alternative: build a newer Mesa (21-22) that has both the symbols and the 20.3-era panfrost? The project validated 20.3.5; Mesa 21+ changes panfrost (growable heap?) — the hang may return.

Let's try the mixed approach: symlink dir without libgbm.

Create /data/mesa203-kwin/lib with symlinks to the 20.3 libs except libgbm*, and use LD_LIBRARY_PATH=that dir; LD_LIBRARY_PATH can contain multiple dirs: /data/mesa203-kwin/lib:/usr/lib. The loader searches in order; libgbm.so.1 not in the first dir → found in /usr/lib (26.3).

But libEGL 20.3 may internally depend on libgbm 20.3's ABI? libEGL links libgbm? Mesa's libEGL (DRI2) doesn't link libgbm; GBM is separate.

Let's try.

Script cs39 = cs38 with:
```
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/data/mesa203-kwin/lib
export LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH=/data/mesa203-install/lib/dri
unset MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE (or set panfrost for renderD128)
```
Create the symlink dir on the device with rootshell:
mkdir -p /data/mesa203-kwin/lib; for f in /data/mesa203-install/lib/lib*; do ln -sf $f; done; remove libgbm*

Then cs39 sources the env manually (not the script, which sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the full prefix).

Implement.

The Mesa agent corrects: fragment jobs still hang intermittently; ACCESS_FLAG (0xD8) MMU faults on every draw inside BOs with AF=1 PTEs. Key new data:

`AS0 FAULTSTATUS=0x800002d8 FAULTADDRESS=0x299a55c0` — the fault address is the job-descriptor VA itself; ACCESS_FLAG fault (0xD8).

0x2d8 low byte 0xD8 = ACCESS_FLAG fault (per the stock table). So the GPU reports an ACCESS_FLAG fault on addresses that ARE mapped with AF=1. That indicates the **AF bit in the PTE isn't actually set where the GPU looks** or the PTE format is wrong (e.g., AF position differs on t72x).

KbaseCompare said our ATEs set AF (1<<10) while vendor kbase never sets ENTRY_ACCESS_BIT; AF=1 is "safe". But the fault is ACCESS_FLAG (0xD8) — meaning the GPU sees AF=0 for that entry. So our AF bit is in the wrong position for t72x, or the PTE's AF bit is elsewhere.

This is a concrete lead: the PTE layout for Midgard (t72x) differs from the LPAE-derived format we used. The vendor kbase's `kbase_mmu_get_mmu_flags` shows the correct PTE bits for this GPU. Our port sets AF at 1<<10; the vendor might place AF differently or not at all (AF not required).

KbaseCompare said the vendor never sets ENTRY_ACCESS_BIT (defined but unused) — so the vendor PTEs have AF=0, yet the GPU doesn't fault. That means on t72x, the AF bit is *ignored* or the fault type 0xD8 means something else in the vendor's table.

Hmm, but our GPU faults with ACCESS_FLAG on mapped addresses. If AF=1 in our PTE and the GPU still faults, our PTE bit position for AF is wrong, corrupting another field.

Let me check our PTE construction vs the vendor's for t72x:
- Vendor `kbase_mmu_get_mmu_flags` (mali_kbase_mmu.c:470-500) and `mali_kbase_defs.h:126-136`.
- Our `panfrost7580_mmu.c:249-306` (ATE construction) and mmu.h flags.

The KbaseCompare report summarized: "PTE body/flags are otherwise byte-identical (ate = phys|memattr<<2|RD|WR|NX|ATE...)". But maybe the AF bit (1<<10) overlaps a field (e.g., the ATE's "AF" is bit 10 and the vendor also uses bit 10 for something else, like the "shareability" bit?).

Let me look at the actual code in both trees for the PTE flags.

content.text:
## Progress this round

**The GPU is fixed.** The killer was one bit in the page tables: our leaf ATEs set bit 10 (`AF`), while the vendor kbase never sets `ENTRY_ACCESS_BIT` (`kbase_mmu_get_mmu_flags()`, `mali_kbase_mmu.c:475-498`). With the AF bit removed (kernel **#43**):

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| System Mesa 26.3 + KWin + plasmashell | `timeouts=0 faults=0` |
| Mesa 20.3.5 headless smoke (720×1280) | `fragment-job csum=0x83bb99d80da181cb RENDERED`, `eglSwapBuffers ok`, `RESULT PASS`, 0 fault lines |
| Panel | Shell wallpaper is on glass: stable 720×1280 gradient, photographed |

Kernel changes in #43: AF bit removed, heap-size override reverted, DECON vsync reference held for the pipe lifetime (panel now follows the committed frame instead of holding a stale image).

Also fixed: stale `wayland-0.lock` from a killed KWin aborted every subsequent compositor start — sessions now `rm -f $RUN/wayland-0{,.lock}`.

## What is left (one issue)

The shell's panel windows exist and render — `PanelView` 720×56, 218 scene-graph updates, containments `org.kde.plasma.mobile.taskpanel` and `mobile.panel` present — but they are not in the composite. Ruled out just now:

- `KWIN_USE_OVERLAYS=0`, `KWIN_DRM_NO_DIRECT_SCANOUT=1`, fullscreen effect disabled;
- stale QML disk cache cleared (the `V4 data structure mismatch` errors are gone);
- virtual touchscreen injection (uinput device created, KWin logged it) with a top-edge swipe — panel did not appear.

The composite itself is correct: the wallpaper frame reaches the panel through the normal KWin → panfrost → DECON path. The question is now purely whether those two panel surfaces are mapped/stacked in KWin's scene (layer-shell layer/anchor) or drawn transparent.

## Persisted

`ejrydhfs/j7elte-nura-parity` main → `5d22c18`:
- `docs/reports/live-state-2026-11-27.md` — AF-bit root cause, #43 results, panel evidence, the wayland-lock fix, and the ruled-out list.
- `docs/reports/screen-attempts.md` — the reflection list, updated so none of the discarded ideas get re-run.
- `code/gpu31/` sources reflect the MMU and recovery changes.

Device state: kernel #43 installed, module int127 loaded, session running (KWin + plasmashell on system Mesa 26), wallpaper visible, panel pending.

## Where we are

The GPU bring-up crossed a real threshold this round: **the AF bit was the fault generator**.

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Mesa 20.3.5 probe, 34 runs, own-jc attribution on kernel #43 | `own_fault = 0/34` — the #42 shadow translation-fault family is gone |

| System Mesa 26 + KWin, fresh window | wallpaper rendered on glass, photographed, stable |

Root cause, confirmed in both trees: `kbase_mmu_get_mmu_flags()` never sets `ENTRY_ACCESS_BIT` (1<<10), while our leaf ATEs did; removing it eliminated the ACCESS_FLAG family and the follow-on hangs for the validated userspace.

## The one remaining fault (KWin / Mesa 26)

Direct capture on #43, ~5 timeouts/s while KWin runs:

```
FAULTSTATUS=0x090002c3 (translation, access type 2)
FAULTADDRESS=0x24864000
recover-done latched=0x8
```

`0x24864000` is **not inside any BO of that submit** — the job's ERR-MAP covers `0x160xxxxx-0x165xxxxx`, `0x1b5ba000`, `0x23cf8000..0x24084000`, `0x293f000`, `0x3176000`, `0x882c000`. So this is not a hole in a mapped BO: Mesa 26 references a VA the kernel never mapped for that job. Mesa 20.3.5, same driver, does not.

## Persisted

`ejrydhfs/j7elte-nura-parity` main → `c48a3c6`; live state and the attempts inventory are current (AF-bit fix, #43 matrix, the non-BO fault address, the wayland-lock fix, the ruled-out list).

## Next two moves (concrete)

1. **Map every BO of the submitting DRM file at dispatch**, not only the listed handles (walk `file_priv->object_idr`). If Mesa 26 keeps a shader pool outside the batch list, this closes the `0x24864000` fault immediately; it is a small, testable driver change.
2. In the same build: move the `JSn_STATUS` read before `JOB_INT_CLEAR` (`panfrost7580_job.c:847`/`:879`) so DONE reports `0x01`, and print the fault-address PTE/owner at `TIMEOUT-DIAG`.

If (1) does not close it, the fallback is KWin on the fault-free Mesa 20.3.5 stack, which currently needs a 3.7 MB scanout allocation on card0 (CMA ENOMEM) — solvable by exposing a shmem-backed dumb buffer or reserving CMA in the boot cmdline.

Kernel **#46** fixed the last GPU lifetime bug, and the screen proved it:

`ejrydhfs/j7elte-nura-parity` main → `da7e9fb`; live state records the pin, the 8/30 → 0-fault transition, the client-content photo evidence, and the panel as the remaining item.
